content: 1. The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) epidemiology and demographics, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. 2. The purpose of this page is to present detailed facts and figures regarding the determinants and distribution of the disease. 3. The page may include a description of the characteristics of the at-risk population, such as gender, race, age, socioeconomic status, dietary habits, geographic location, and environmental conditions. 4. It should also provide data on the distribution of the disease burden within the population. 5. At the top of the edit box, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template you created earlier. 6. Ensure that links within the page are specific and direct readers to the most relevant pages. For example, if the term anterior spinal artery syndrome is mentioned, the link should direct to the page for anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. 7. Follow the formatting and capitalization guidelines outlined in the provided template. 8. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. Overview 9. The overview section must include the disease name in the first sentence. 10. This section should summarize the page in a few sentences and may overlap with the epidemiology and demographics section on the main overview page. Prevalence 11. Prevalence is defined as the total number of cases of a disease in a specific at-risk population at a given time. 12. When reporting numbers with decimal points, limit them to one digit after the decimal to avoid creating a false sense of precision. 13. Use template sentences to describe prevalence, such as: Worldwide, the prevalence of (disease) ranges from a low of ___ per 100,000 persons to a high of ___ per 100,000 persons, with an average prevalence of ___ per 100,000 persons. In developed countries, the prevalence of (disease) ranges from ___ to ___ per 100,000 persons. In developing countries, the prevalence of (disease) is ___ per 100,000 persons. 14. If specific data is available for a particular year, include it, e.g., In (year), the prevalence of (disease) was estimated to be ___ cases per 100,000 individuals worldwide. Incidence 15. Incidence refers to the number of new cases of a disease in a population over a specific time period. 16. The standard format for reporting incidence is ___ per 100,000 individuals. 17. Avoid reporting more than one digit after the decimal point to maintain clarity and avoid false precision. 18. Use template sentences to describe incidence, such as: Worldwide, the incidence of (disease) ranges from ___ to ___ per 100,000 persons, with an average incidence of ___ per 100,000 persons. In developed countries, the incidence of (disease) is ___ per 100,000 persons. In developing countries, the incidence of (disease) is ___ per 100,000 persons. 19. If specific data is available for a particular year, include it, e.g., In (year), the incidence of (disease) was estimated to be ___ cases per 100,000 individuals worldwide. Case Fatality Rate 20. The case fatality rate (CFR) is defined as the proportion of deaths among individuals diagnosed with the disease. 21. CFR should not be confused with the mortality rate, which refers to the number of deaths in the at-risk population. 22. When reporting percentages, limit decimal points to one digit to avoid false precision. 23. Use template sentences to describe CFR, such as: In (year), the case fatality rate of (disease) was ___%. The annual case fatality rate of (disease) is approximately ___%. Age 24. This section should describe how the disease affects individuals of different age groups and provide age-specific prevalence and incidence data. 25. Use template sentences such as: The prevalence of (disease) increases/decreases with age. (Acute disease) commonly affects (specific age group). (Chronic disease) is usually first diagnosed among (specific age group). Gender 26. This section should describe how the prevalence of the disease varies by gender. 27. When reporting male-to-female ratios, limit decimal points to one digit to avoid false precision. 28. Use template sentences such as: (Gender 1) are more commonly affected by (disease) than (gender 2), with a male-to-female ratio of approximately ___ to 1. The prevalence and incidence of (disease) do not vary by gender. Men and women are equally affected by (disease). Race 29. This section should describe how the disease differs based on race. 30. Use template sentences such as: The prevalence of (disease) does not vary by race. (Disease) is more prevalent in (specific race) compared to (other race). There is no racial predilection for (disease). Developed Countries 31. This section should describe the impact of the disease in developed countries, including incidence, prevalence, and geographic distribution. 32. Mention any societal impacts of the disease in these regions. Developing Countries 33. This section should describe the impact of the disease in developing countries, including incidence, prevalence, and geographic distribution. 34. Highlight any societal impacts of the disease in these regions. Preferred Template Statements 35. If the incidence or prevalence of the disease is known, use statements such as: The incidence/prevalence of (disease) is approximately ___ per 100,000 individuals worldwide. In (year), the incidence/prevalence of (disease) was estimated to be ___ cases per 100,000 individuals worldwide. 36. If the case fatality rate is also known, use statements such as: The incidence of (disease) is approximately ___ per 100,000 individuals, with a case fatality rate of ___%. 37. If details about prevalence by age, race, or gender are known, include them in the appropriate sections. For example: The incidence of (disease) increases with age; the median age at diagnosis is ___ years. (Disease) commonly affects individuals younger than/older than ___ years of age. There is no racial predilection for (disease). (Disease) affects men and women equally. 38. If regional prevalence data is available, include statements such as: The majority of cases are reported in (specific region). 39. Include any additional details about the patient population typically diagnosed with the disease.
